lens: QUANT SKEPTIC. I judged each design on its edge after all costs: swap fee, tx fee, impact at realistic size under both impact bounds, and shielded N+2 latency. I also judged capacity, evidence quality, data-snooping and overfitting risk, regime dependence, survivorship and netuid-splice bias, and whether each falsification test has the statistical power to settle anything. My default prior was "no edge". I read the full brief and checked key numbers against the corpus. The corpus shows the factor replication used T/A prices, 7,200-block daily samples, ±100% winsorisation and started subnets ≥7 d old, with long-short EW terciles, zero entry lag and naive IC t-stats.

evaluations.strengths: Most mechanism-grounded design. It attacks the brief's central open question (the sign of total return) in the right units: simple TAO returns, P×I, net of costs, generation-keyed, dissolution payouts included. Its building blocks are verified: the closed-form yield matches to 3 digits, the emission replica matches to ~2e-7, and the injection-cap algebra holds. The derived threshold G(b) ≥ 1.526·rp·(p/EMA)/(1−burn) is correct (I re-derived it). It rightly shows that young high-rp micro caps get price-neutral injection, not a protocol bid, and so it rightly demotes gate-boundary trading to a tilt. Sizing V* = y(μH−2f)/4 checks out (y=3,000, μ=0.3%/d, H=7 gives 15 TAO and ≈0.14%/d net). It reports both impact bounds, and low turnover (5–21 d holds) keeps cost drag near 0.1%/day. The expected-edge statement is honest: unconditional ≈+0.01%/day, 45% bear case. It isolates the one near-certain sub-component: a take-0 hotkey with realised ΔlnI tracking. T3 (cross-section of ~100 subnets × 66–107 d) and T6 have real power. It openly admits T4(b) can only reject disasters, and it caps the tuned-parameter budget.
evaluations.fatal_or_major_flaws:
1) The economic thesis rests on one unverified assumption: that the sell-load screen lifts the book 0.25–0.55 pts/day above universe drift. The illustration table and the '≈1%/day dispersion' claim are a one-parameter plausibility check with assumed φ.
2) T3 is not identified as written. k_w·S/y ∝ AE·p/y = AE/x is mechanically an inverse-size variable, so any small/young/dying-subnet outflow pattern loads on β. That pattern is exactly the documented negative SMB plus prune fear. Passing T3 would not show that emission recipients sell; it could just rediscover 'small loses'.
3) The benchmark is too weak. T4 compares against the EW universe; the screen has to beat a trivial yield×size (or age) double sort, or the sell-load machinery adds nothing.
4) It is over-built for the evidence: forward chain-buy simulator, reflexive-loop tilt (+0.03%/d derived), event module, drain timing, basket overhang, market intercept. That is ~45 parameters. The '6 tuned' budget ignores structural thresholds chosen after reading the brief's statistics, and every module's effect is below 0.05%/d, undetectable in ~66 rank-32-gate days.
5) The market intercept m_mkt = clip(1+α0/0.5%, 0, 1) is a lagging market-timing filter. If the sell-load model does not absorb the gate-era −0.46%/d drift, then α0 ≈ −0.4 and the book sits near-flat most of the time.
6) The acceptance tests lack power. T12 (30 days, net ≥ 0) is a coin flip: with a ~3%/day book SD, the SE of a 30-day mean is ≈0.55%/day against a 0.05–0.1 edge. T9 sign stability over ~35-day sub-periods is noise.
7) There is zero in-regime history. Spec 475 (2026-10-07) changed dividend and emission code ('precise emissions', Null consensus), so the closed form, injection cap and φ's all need re-verification.
8) Capacity may be overstated. rho_in 2.0 plus rank_in 8, while ladder ranks 4–15 sit at 1.53–1.70×, may exclude most sub-3,000-TAO pools. That pushes the book into 3,000–8,000-TAO pools paying 0.1–0.3%/d yield.
9) dd_stop marks at spot × I, which own impact inflates by ~V/T. It should mark at executable value.

Every module must beat this number out of sample.

Estimate φ_o and φ_m directly from owner-coldkey and miner-coldkey StakeRemoved flows (events, or Taostats stake-events once the key arrives); keep the regression as a cross-check only. The screen must beat a yield×size double sort out of sample.

evaluations.fatal_or_major_flaws:
1) Cost-model bug. candidate() computes RT by selling the bought alpha back into the post-buy pool. In a CPMM that returns ≈V(1−f)², so RT ≈ 2f + tx and the 2V/T impact that the narrative and sizing assume disappears. The coded gate is the optimistic (persistent-impact) bound and over-admits trades by ~0.2–0.6% per trade.
2) The evidence does not map to the tradable strategy:
- the stats are long-short, EW terciles, daily rebalanced, over all started subnets (dying names drive REV), zero entry lag, gross;
- the IC t-stats are naive, and the gate-era +0.77%/d spread was never re-run;
- long-leg-only and N≈30 thin-universe effects are unmeasured, and F2 needs ~200 days this regime does not have.
3) The net edge is mostly carry. Central EH = 2.5 d × (−0.25 + 0.40) + 0.275% alpha, so half the gross is yield minus drift: the flow-yield thesis at higher turnover. Momentum alpha of 0.14–0.25%/d, against RT of 0.4–0.65% per ~2-day hold (0.2–0.33%/d) plus ≈0.14%/d turnover drag, is ≤ 0 net on its own.
4) Several features have no evidence: impulse path P1, ema_gap, struct_lag, blow-off trim, and the breadth gate. The weekly-reversal guard is calibrated on the dead Taoflow regime. Around 40 knobs create large researcher degrees of freedom despite 'tune 4'.
5) Intraday continuation is untested. A 12-min scan plus shielded N+2 means unshielded bots capture the front of any impulse.
6) Capacity is 20–100 TAO with central profit of 3–8 TAO/yr. The F6 portfolio criteria (≥60% of ~5–8 test windows positive) have no power.

evaluations.strengths:
The most intellectually honest design:
- The premise check is right: the AMM has no restoring force and impact does not decay, so only opposing flow can revert a move.
- It quantifies the mechanical refill at ≤5–10% of an 8% shock, and zero below the gate.
- It lists correctly where reversion is not expected: daily REV, claim bursts, the drain sawtooth, owner dumps, slow EMA dips.
The self-disabling edge gate starts from a below-break-even prior (ρ0 = 0.15, pseudo-n 20), so it cannot trade on hope. Its test protocol is the best in the set:
- pre-registered power floor (N ≥ 80 / ≥ 40);
- Bonferroni across horizons, matched-block placebos, latency decay F7, falling-knife audit F8;
- deflated Sharpe and CSCV with only 4 tuned parameters, and regime consistency checks.
The break-even arithmetic is correct (c ≈ 1.2% at α = 0.5%, T = 1,500; ρ* = 0.25 at D = 8%).
evaluations.fatal_or_major_flaws:
1) There is no positive evidence. The closest evidence points the other way: 1-day REV −0.53 to −0.57 (t ≈ −3, i.e. continuation), small-tercile drift around −0.6%/d, and dips clustering in dying and diluted subnets (adverse selection).
2) It needs ≥25% behavioural recovery within 12 h, after a 2-minute stabilisation wait plus N+2 latency. The sellers may be informational and are indistinguishable on chain: split owner sales, compromised wallets, news.
3) The economics are tiny. Profit per event is T(g−c0)²/8 ≈ 0.05–0.25 TAO, useful capital is 10–50 TAO, and the optimistic case is +0.4–2.5 TAO/month before knife-tail losses. Stops are porous (2–3% exit slippage) and a prune pays 0.35–0.65×.
4) Event frequency is unknown. With the filtered universe at 6–20 names (90-day age, E/x ≤ 0.2, cushion ≥ 0.30), the N ≥ 40 power floor may never be reached in the gate era, so the likeliest outcome is 'insufficient power, stay SHADOW' forever.
5) It carries the highest engineering burden for the least likely edge: per-block System.Events decoding (scalecodec on Windows unverified), flow labels, claim signatures, owner sets, two-endpoint agreement and per-block shadow logging.
6) The FORCED and WHALE labels are unvalidated heuristics, and the calibration cells fragment an already small sample.

- Do not build the trading module or its per-block shadow pipeline.
- If the question still matters, run a one-off offline event study instead. Use state_queryStorage change-sets for SubnetTAO, SubnetAlphaIn and SwapBalancer on the ~40 band subnets over the gate era (a few hundred archive calls). Measure F1 recovery ρ_H at 1, 6 and 12 h against matched placebo blocks, F7 latency decay, and F9 pump symmetry, all with the pre-registered thresholds.

evaluations.fatal_or_major_flaws:
1) LCW's edge rests on an unmeasured input. The 1–4%/day early dividend yield is a closed-form extrapolation to a tiny A_earn. Permit allocation, bond-EMA lag under classic Yuma, the default 18% take, and the yield compression caused by the very inflows LCW requires are all unquantified.
2) LCW can never be validated. At ~5–10 qualifying trades a year, its own FT4 rule leaves it paper-only indefinitely. Expected value is 1–4 TAO/yr, with ≥40% probability of a non-positive mean.
3) Requiring early inflow (φ ≥ +0.4%/day) selects exactly the temporary-demand phase that the cohort data show reversing after about day 30. The flat d7/d14 median also has weaknesses:
- it is measured from first-move prices;
- it pools regimes (Era-B launches started with emission on);
- n ≈ 21 with common calendar shocks.
4) L2 snipe is structurally late (shielded N+2..N+4 vs unshielded bots) against a +6% median 14-day max run-up. Mode I has 2 historical events, and the right-tail scorecard is unpowered by construction. All three add code with roughly zero expected value.
5) The Gatekeeper's avoided-loss estimate (+0.1–0.3%/d) comes from the pre-gate cohort and overlaps the other sleeves' own 30–90-day age filters. Its marginal value is being the single implementation, not new alpha. Its DILUTED flag also uses yet another sell-load parameterisation (f_o = f_m = 0.8, κ_d = 0.25).

evaluations.fatal_or_major_flaws:
1) It embeds untested alpha models as hard vetoes and haircuts. TRD_BAN (−0.75%/d), m_trd, m_gate and LAMBDA_SELL re-implement the flow-yield sell-load model with different parameters. If FT4 fails, the overlay will already have removed the exposure the sleeves exist to test, and ablations will be confounded.
2) Tier A coverage is overstated. With a ≈ 0.000276–0.000286 and U + M_A = 159 blocks, Tier A covers EMA gaps of only ≈2.2% under a 50% spot crash and ≈4.5% at zero price, not ~4% and ~6%. So most protection rests on Tier B and the backstop, which in turn rest on:
- guessed jump parameters (JUMP_P, JUMP_SIZE, σ floor);
- a 32-interval hazard table that is regime-dependent (hot-market openings, spec-475 PoW registration, a possible SubnetLimit change).
3) FT1's out-of-sample recall test uses 26 events. 25/26 has a 95% CI of roughly 80–100%, so it cannot tell a good guard from a mediocre one. Precision costs (backstop exits lasting 1.5–3 days per registration cycle) could dominate for sleeves exposed to the ladder.
4) On correlated long-only micro caps (book SD ~3–4%/day), DAILY_LOSS 6% trips on ~2–7% of days and DD_SOFT/DD_HARD will bind often, so the portfolio risks sitting in CAUTION permanently. Inverse-vol budgets after 60 paper days across highly correlated sleeves would be noise.
5) There is no single portfolio market-regime throttle; the sleeves carry four different ones. There is also no regime burn-in after a spec that changes emission or dividend logic, and 475 was one.
6) Complexity is high: ~40 parameter groups and a 2,000-path MC every 60 blocks, each threshold a governance-dependent constant that can go stale.

cross_cutting:
1) THE LEVEL EDGE IS NOT IDENTIFIABLE FROM P&L.
- The central net edges are 0.03–0.1%/day. Book SD is ~2–4%/day; tracking error vs the EW universe is ~1.5–2%/day.
- At those numbers, a t=2 on the level needs years of data (≈1,400–5,600 days).
- So 30–60-day paper 'net ≥ 0' gates are coin flips, and portfolio-level backtest gates (60% of windows positive, etc.) have no power.
- Promotion must rest on component tests that do have power: cross-sectional ICs with entry lag, realised vs predicted hotkey yield, realised vs predicted structural drift, realised vs modelled cost and fill rate, prune-guard recall and precision. P&L tests can only kill on disasters.

2) THERE IS NO IN-REGIME HISTORY.
- The rank-32 gate has run about 66 days. Spec 475 (2026-10-07) changed dividend and emission code; 476 is pending.
- Every backtest is therefore out-of-regime by construction, and post-475 paper data is the only true out-of-sample.
- Pre-register and freeze all thresholds, not only the 'tuned' ones. Control multiple testing across all five designs (~150+ knobs, many variants and ablations) with deflated Sharpe or CSCV at project level.

3) THE EVIDENCE BASE NEEDS RE-RUNNING BEFORE IT IS USED AS PRIORS.
- The SMB, WML, REV and IC numbers are price-only, long-short, EW daily-rebalanced, on T/A prices (biased for v3-era micro caps), over all started subnets, at zero lag.
- The corpus does not say whether prune days were booked at the dissolution payout, or how netuid-generation splices were handled under ±100% winsorisation. A splice-day jump could bias the small tercile by tenths of a percent per day.
- EW daily rebalancing in a continuation regime also differs from low-turnover holding.
- Rebuild one generation-keyed, payout-inclusive P×I panel. Re-run the factors on it, and benchmark every sleeve at its own turnover.

4) USE ONE FILL MODEL AND ONE MARKING RULE.
- In a CPMM, own impact persists unless someone trades against it. An immediate round trip on own impact returns about V minus fees, which is what momentum's candidate() computes. The temporary-impact bound costs about 2V/T.
- The backtester should replay historical reserves with our own trades injected, and report both bounds.
- Gate and size on the conservative bound. Fill shielded orders at the block N+2 state, with misses and failed-order fees.
- Mark every position and stop at executable sim_sell value, never at spot. Spot marking inflates P&L by about V/T.

5) BUILD ONE STRUCTURAL SELL-LOAD AND EMISSION MODULE.
- Five designs parameterise the same untested model differently:
  - flow-yield: φ_o/φ_m 0.8/0.6;
  - momentum: ψ_s 0.5;
  - overlay: LAMBDA_SELL 0.5;
  - launch: f_o/f_m 0.8/0.8 plus κ_d;
  - mean reversion: assumes all of it is sold.
- Left as is, one unverified assumption vetoes names four times, and ablation becomes impossible.
- Calibrate it once: control T3 for size, age and rp, and measure coldkey-level owner and miner sells directly from events. Apply it in exactly one place, and keep it monitoring-only in the overlay until FT4/T3 pass.

6) ONE GUARD SET, AND A HONEST UNIVERSE COUNT.
- The overlay owns prune, emission, owner and age logic; sleeves may only be stricter.
- Stacked filters may shrink the real sub-3,000-TAO universe to a handful of names: age 30–90 d, immunity, ρ ≥ 1.5–2.0× bottom EMA, burn caps, E/x caps, emission-on, T bands.
- Count eligible names at ≥10 historical dates before building. If micro caps mostly vanish, say so: the project is then trading 3,000–8,000-TAO pools at lower yield.

7) CAPACITY AND RISK ARE SHARED.
- All sleeves draw on the same ~20 pools. Total project capacity is about 100–250 TAO, not per sleeve; the allocator's per-netuid sum-then-cap is essential.
- The sleeves are one long-only micro-cap factor, so cross-sleeve diversification is mostly illusory.
- There are four market-regime throttles: m_mkt, breadth/m_u, the MR breadth halt, and the DD governors. Replace them with one in the overlay.
- Fund sleeves by evidence stage, not by inverse-vol.

8) WHAT THE ALLOCATOR MUST HANDLE:
- forced-exit priority across sleeves;
- netting at spot, with un-netted attribution for kill switches;
- per-netuid aggregate caps, with the overlay veto winning when sleeves conflict on the same netuid;
- one hotkey per (coldkey, netuid) via a shared YieldRouter, to avoid dust;
- fee buffers;
- strict paper/live separation. Nothing in this process executes live orders.

9) EVENT-DRIVEN SCOPE.
- Per-block reaction is justified for risk only: Tier A prune exits, emission-off, owner events, SafeMode, reconciliation.
- Every alpha signal is daily or slower (daily evidence, 8 h EMA). Alpha sleeves should decide hourly to daily.
- This cuts RPC load on a host with no Docker or WSL for a lite node, and shrinks the attack and failure surface. Mean reversion is the only per-block alpha, and it is the weakest.

10) RECOMMENDED BUILD ORDER.
- (i) Shared reader, 60-block generation-keyed panel, P×I index, fill simulator and emission/yield replica, re-verified post-475.
- (ii) Overlay prune engine plus FT1 per-block replay.
- (iii) Baseline EW total-return answer to open question #3.
- (iv) Flow-yield MVP in paper, with component tests.
- (v) Offline-only studies: momentum IC with lag and long leg, launch FT1/FT2, and the mean-reversion event study. Promote only on pre-registered passes.

lens:
PROTOCOL MECHANICS. Each formula and assumption was checked against RESEARCH_BRIEF.md (read in full) and spot-checked in verified_corpus.json / critique_and_gapfill.json. Areas checked:
- emission gate, EMA alpha and half-life
- injection cap vs chain buys, alpha_out split, dividend / share-price mechanics
- prune rule and dissolution payout
- limit-price marginal semantics, fees, min-stake / dust rules, event semantics
- sensitivity to governance parameters
- reliance on stale fields (BlockEmission, DynamicInfo.emission, SubnetEmaTaoFlow)

Corpus facts used beyond the brief:
- SubnetOwnerCut is a global StorageValue (unset on chain, so the default 11,796 applies).
- transition_stake_internal charges the swap fee on the origin leg only (destination fee dropped).
- Before 8,466,531, get_ema_flow reset SubnetTaoFlow every block. SubnetTaoFlow is recorded only in stake_into_subnet / unstake_from_subnet / collateral, so chain buys are almost certainly not in it.
- Share denominator: use TotalHotkeyShares V1 if present, else V2, per (hotkey, netuid), up to block 9,217,507.
- SubnetFastMovingPrice is a basket-era item, updated from the previous block's end spot.
- NetworkRegistrationQueued fields {coldkey, hotkey, mechid, identity, lock_amount, median_subnet_alpha_price, registration_block} are confirmed. The new netuid comes from get_next_netuid (lowest free id, skipping ids in DissolveCleanupQueue).

evaluations.strengths:
This is the most mechanically faithful design.

Verified correct:
- Spot p=(w1/w2)y/x, k_w=1/w_base, post-buy spot p(1+dy/y)^(1/w1), post-sell p(1+dx/x)^(-1/w2). Both limit formulas are post-fill MARGINAL prices with a margin, which is the correct limit semantics.
- Emission vector matches get_shares exactly:
  - b over the eligible set, theta = Nth-largest positive b, Hill gate h.
  - Disabled subnets keep their rank and are zeroed after the gate, then renormalised.
  - Block emission comes from the runtime, never BlockEmission storage.
- Injection cap 7200*rp*alpha_emission*p, with chain buys CB=max(0,E-cap).
- Derived CB threshold G>=1.526*rp*(p/EMA)/(1-burn) is right. I re-derived the b/theta table (0.63/0.76/0.95/1.16/1.48/4.97). So CB>0 is impossible at spot≈EMA for rp>=0.655. This correctly kills the 'gate-boundary chain-buy support' story for young micro caps. The corollary (CB rises after a spot drop because cap tracks spot while E tracks EMA) is also correct.
- EMA a=SubnetMovingAlpha*b/(b+EMAPriceHalvingBlocks), b from FirstEmissionBlockNumber-1. Linearised reflexive loop is correct up to a dropped kappa*lambda term in the characteristic equation; immaterial.
- alpha_out split: 18% owner / 0.41 miners*(1-burn) / 0.41*rp root into baskets, gated on the Σ EMA>1 root flag / 0.41*(1-rp) compounding.
- Closed-form yield 2952(1-rp)/A_earn, with A_earn = sum over AlphaDividendsPerSubnet keys (not AlphaOut).
- Default take 18% for absent Delegates.
- 'Dilution already in P, never subtract twice.'
- Drain timing: stake at <=B-1 earns, unstake landing in B keeps credit, shielded N+2. The non-urgent exit delay to land >=B is correct.
- move_stake u64::MAX semantics; same-subnet move has no swap fee.
- Prune rule (min EMA, tie earliest reg) excluding immune subnets; never hold get_subnet_to_prune target.
- Dissolution haircut E/(x+E).
- Explicitly bans SubnetEmaTaoFlow and the sdk subnet_tao_flows().
- Dust rules: full exit exempt, 0.02 TAO remainder, 0.002 TAO partial output.
- Spec-change pause and model-health check.
evaluations.fatal_or_major_flaws:
No fatal mechanics errors.

Major:
(1) SubnetOwnerCut is listed among 'Identity u16 netuid keys'. It is a global StorageValue (unset, so default 11,796). A per-netuid key will read absent. The behaviour when OwnerCutEnabled=false is unverified: the design assumes the 18% is redistributed via (1-c_o) to miners.
(2) Historical hotkey index I uses 'TotalHotkeySharesV2 (legacy for old blocks)'. In the whole gate era (8.04M-9.217M) the correct denominator is V1 if present, else V2, per (hotkey, netuid). Otherwise T4/T6/T12 total returns are wrong exactly in the test window.
(3) Spec 475 ('precise emissions', Null consensus, PoW registration) went live 2026-10-07; it is not a future event. c_E, T2 and the yield closed form must be re-verified on post-475 blocks before paper trading; 476 is the pending one.
(4) Prune hazard:
  - The registration CDF is in raw blocks, so it breaks if NetworkLockReductionInterval, block emission or NetworkRateLimit change.
  - The extra 0.5x scaling when cost >1.2L double-counts information already in time-since-registration.
  - There is no prune_possible (SubnetLimit + DissolveCleanupQueue) gate.
(5) The gate tilt band rank_b in [22,45] is absolute; it must move with the live EmissionBarRank N.

Minor:
- E_obs=SubnetTaoInEmission+SubnetExcessTao undercounts when injection is parked in Balancer reservoirs, so the health check can fail spuriously.
- c_E (≈4,718) is a cross-sectional quantity 3600/(Z·Σ bG), not a constant.
- 'Burn>=0.9 gets zero TAO' should read MB>=1 exactly zero, MB 0.9 near-zero via the gate.
- A_earn grows mechanically by ≈0.41·7200·alpha_out/day (escrow deposits credited in place to validator hotkeys while Σ EMA>1, plus compounding). This is only captured empirically via gA.
- E_b history exists only from v441 (8,765,683); a reconstruction method is unstated.
- ΔSubnetTaoFlow excludes chain buys (not recorded on that path) but includes claim_root sales and collateral buys. Verify, so T1/T3 decompositions are not mis-specified.
- NetworkRegistrationAllowed=false freezes the EMA; the prune projection should treat a=0.

- momentum: excl rank ≤6 / exit rank ≤3
- mean-reversion: cushion 0.30, rank 6
- launch: immunity backstop

lens: ENGINEERING: data availability and historical reconstructability, event-driven implementability within public RPC limits (~1-3 req/s, OnFinality free tier 400k RU/day), determinism and testability, and how faithfully a backtest can simulate own impact, N+2 latency, yield accrual and dissolution payouts. Basket escrow exists only from v441 (block 8,765,683). One state_queryStorageAt with 2,332 keys takes about 0.45 s. state_queryStorage over 100 blocks x 384 keys took 24.5 s / 2.95 MB on OnFinality public. - the model_ok gate halts entries when the two diverge, which matters right now because spec 475 'precise emissions' and Null consensus went live yesterday.

The falsification ladder works component by component (T1 flow identity, T2 emission model, T3 sell load), so cheap tests can kill expensive modules before they are built. (2) Data-statement error. data_requirements says SubnetTaoFlow is valid 'from the Taoflow storage start'. It is a valid running total only from block 8,466,531; before that it was reset every block. Proxy(move_stake_limit) fees are unmeasured; only swap_stake_limit at 0.00125 is known. This invites a sim-vs-live mismatch.

(4) SubnetFastMovingPrice only has basket-era history, so chain_macd cold start is unavailable for most of the sample. The nf fallback before 8,466,531 rebuilds flow from an emission model during a period when chain buys were unrecorded (before spec 411).
(5) F2 on the tradable universe (N about 30) needs about 200 independent days; the gate era has about 66. Universe-restricted tests can only reject.
(6) The P1 out-of-cycle trigger and 2-entries-per-scan rule collide with the overlay's one-in-flight-per-netuid rule and its 3-delegate nonce budget.

- Make the default fill the next feasible block: decision +2/+3 from per-block reads when available, otherwise the next 60-block snapshot. Report decision-state fills only as an upper bound.
- Ship the MVP first: S_mvp + cost gate + hysteresis + adaptive min-hold. No P1, no gap or struct terms, no rotation.
- Keep P1 disabled until F14 shows edge surviving to t+3 blocks.

evaluations.strengths:
- Safe by construction: it defaults to SHADOW, and its prior (rho0 = 0.15) sits below break-even, so no order is possible until shadow data earns it.
- Uses the exact per-block pool identity r = 2 ln(1+phi) as a data-quality filter.
- Restricts exact math to Era C, keys by generation, and uses worst-of-two-states N+2 fills, 2% order misses, a latency-decay test (F7), matched placebos (F4) and a pre-registered 4-parameter tuning set.
- Live load is tiny: about 2 calls per block, or 0.17 req/s.
- The shock_log and block recorder are a reusable microstructure dataset. It can calibrate the overlay's N+2 beta buffers and limit margins for every sleeve.
evaluations.fatal_or_major_flaws:
(1) The block-level backfill rests on a false premise.
- Any enabled subnet with a positive burn-adjusted share receives a nonzero injection every block, even far below the gate (g > 0), and Swap weights are re-solved on every injection.
- So SubnetTAO, SubnetAlphaIn and SwapBalancer change every block. state_queryStorage returns every block for essentially the whole eligible universe; only disabled or MinerBurned >= 1 subnets change only on trades.
- At the measured 100 blocks x 384 keys per 24.5 s, the gate era is about 5,000 range calls, 10-30 h and several GB, not 'a few hundred range calls'.
(2) The Stage-1 screen selects on outcome. Flagging windows where ln(P_t/P_{t-60}) <= -4% drops exactly the shocks that recovered within 60 blocks. That biases rho, eps and the CAL cells, and the edge gate depends on those cells.
(3) Labels (OWNER, FORCED, WHALE) need System.Events decoded against per-spec metadata (scalecodec on Windows is unverified). ROUND_TRIP needs 48-hour coldkey ledgers that only Taostats can supply.
(4) Live per-block detection needs gap-free head coverage. A throttled or late public endpoint silently corrupts the 1-25-block shock windows.
(5) The E/x filter has history only from 8,765,683.
(6) Calibration needs at least 80 shocks and 15-20 per cell. Event frequency is unknown, so the module may sit uncalibrated for months.
The economic prior (REV negative, daily losers continue) means the expected value of this build is mainly the dataset, not a trading sleeve.
evaluations.required_changes:
- Use dSubnetTaoFlow as the trade-timing index. After 8,466,531 it changes only on user stake and unstake. A state_queryStorage over the 128 SubnetTaoFlow keys returns only trade blocks.
  - Detect shocks from single-block flow phi, so there is no outcome selection.
  - Then pull pool state with state_queryStorageAt at t-1 .. t+H only for candidate windows.
- Measure OnFinality range-call limits before sizing the backfill.
- On a head gap, catch up through the ~300 blocks of state that lite nodes keep. Mark windows with missing blocks as invalid rather than interpolating.
- Arm A stays SHADOW until F15 and F1 pass. Arms B, C, D and O are shadow-only permanently unless their own tests pass.
- Build after the core infrastructure, reusing the shared recorder, identity invariant and event decoder.
- Feed the latency and refill measurements to the risk overlay's order planner. This is the most likely durable value.

evaluations.strengths:
The Launch Gatekeeper is cheap, exact and highly reusable:
- Generation registry from NetworkRegisteredAt diffs (binary search, about 6 calls each) plus the 52 NetworkRegistrationQueued events, with seed-state assertions: Queued-to-Added lag 17-25, SubnetTAO == lock, netuid == victim.
- start_call detection by storage diff.
- Dense recorder windows via change-set range calls (about 20k calls for 52 launches).
- A deterministic flag API that every other family needs: UNSTARTED, EMA_WARMING, DILUTED, BURNING, EMISSION_OFF, generation boundaries, immunity calendar.
The closed-form EMA forecast is unit-tested against the exact recursion. The design is honest about sample size: LCW stays paper-only below 8 qualifying trades. FT5 measures start_call latency curves at block level, and there is an explicit never-trade list. Live load is tiny: per-block polling only for WAIT_START, WATCH and HELD generations.
evaluations.fatal_or_major_flaws:
(1) LCW cannot be validated with the available history. Cohort C has about 21 launches, about 9-11 born under the gate, none past day 90. FT4 will almost surely return 'not testable', so months of forward recording come before any paper verdict.
(2) The miner-quality and permit gates need per-epoch metagraph data. get_selective_metagraph needs per-runtime type metadata (13-51 KB per call), and the low-level storage names (Incentive, ValidatorPermit, Keys, Owner) are unverified in the corpus.
(3) Owner and buyer-breadth history for each launch's first 14 days needs StakeAdded/StakeRemoved events across about 100k blocks per launch. That is infeasible on the public archive, and the Taostats key is pending.
(4) The NetworkRegistrationQueued field layout and the units of median_subnet_alpha_price depend on the runtime and are unverified.
(5) The registration_clock and hazard duplicate the risk overlay's, with different smoothing and tail rules.
(6) The exclusion policy (the flow family excludes YOUNG_IMMUNE, under 120 days since registration) contradicts the flow design's min_age of 45 days since start_call.
evaluations.required_changes:
- Build the Gatekeeper (registry, recorder, flags) now as shared infrastructure.
- Delete its separate registration clock and consume the overlay's hazard API.
- LCW goes behind a flag, paper only, enabled only after FT0-FT2 pass on the forward-recorded cohort. Owner pressure comes from per-epoch AlphaV2 diffs of the owner coldkey on SubnetOwnerHotkey; miner metrics come from storage items verified against metadata; events are enrichment only.

evaluations.strengths:
The most complete and most correct component. Highlights:
- Per-block prune engine using the exact victim rule (52/52), cross-checked against get_subnet_to_prune every block.
- Stressed t* EMA projection compared with the unwind time (U = 9 blocks plus M_A); registration window from LastRateLimitedBlock(0x02); prune_possible from SubnetLimit and DissolveCleanupQueue.
- Recovery formula reproduces SN92's 0.368.
- The CPMM path-independence argument (tranching helps only with chain-buy refill) is correct and saves fees.
- Liquidation-marked NAV; N+2 drift buffers estimated from data; dust and remainder rules; delegate fee buffers.
- A NORMAL / CAUTION / EXITS_ONLY / FROZEN mode machine, with the V1-V7 spec-change validation suite and runtime-API fallbacks for exits.
- Stake, proxy and nonce reconciliation, and FT11 fault drills.
Every threshold has a falsification test: FT1 out-of-sample on prunes 27-52 with per-block EMA validation on the last 10, FT10 payout replay. Gross alpha is defined as zero, so it is judged only by the ON vs OFF ablation (FT5).
evaluations.fatal_or_major_flaws:
(1) The Monte Carlo P_prune is unseeded. Backtests, unit tests and Tier B decisions are non-deterministic and can flip from run to run.
(2) There is no explicit backtest execution model shared with the sleeves. Fills at N+2 from per-block state vs 60-block snapshots, failure injection and fee table are specified only for paper (FT7).
(3) The planner lacks a cross-subnet Rotate (move_stake_limit) order type, which momentum depends on. It also lacks a priority class for time-critical sleeve entries, such as mean reversion's 10-block window, under one-in-flight-per-netuid and 3 delegates.
(4) Double haircut: m_gate, m_trd and TRD_BAN reapply a dilution model (LAMBDA_SELL = 0.5) to sleeves that already net sell load with their own calibrated parameters (flow phi_o = 0.8, phi_m = 0.6). A name can be zeroed by two inconsistent models.
(5) 'Never split one subnet across hotkeys' conflicts with each sleeve's own choose_hotkey and take_max (0.02 / 0.05 / argmax marginal).
(6) The live design assumes an own lite node and at least 2 healthy endpoints. The host cannot run a node (no Docker or WSL), so paper relies on OnFinality keyed plus public endpoints.
(7) The first version is large: MC, Tier B, inverse-vol allocator and virtual netting all come before any sleeve has evidence.

cross_cutting:
1. SHARED INFRASTRUCTURE (build once, before any sleeve)
(a) ChainReader. Custom JSON-RPC client:
- twox128/xxh64/blake2_128 key builders;
- decoders for u64, i64, I96F32, U64F64, U96F32, Perquintill, SafeFloat, Option and bool;
- absent-key defaults from that block's metadata, cached per spec;
- raw-response archiving for reproducibility.
(b) One StateView per block: a single state_queryStorageAt of about 1,300-1,600 keys (128 netuids x ~10 items, plus Swap weights and fees, plus globals). This is the same object in backtest, paper and live.
(c) DuckDB/Parquet store keyed by (netuid, NetworkRegisteredAt, block).
(d) The §2.7 pool simulator.
(e) ONE emission/gate/EMA/injection-cap replica, unit-tested against SubnetTaoInEmission+SubnetExcessTao. Four designs each re-implement it today.
(f) ONE sell-load/dilution model. Today there are five (flow S_n with phi 0.8/0.6, momentum dp with psi_s 0.5, launch sell_overhang 0.8/0.8, overlay D_n with LAMBDA_SELL 0.5, mean-reversion dilution_load). Calibrate it once in flow's T3 and share the parameters.
(g) ONE prune ladder, t*, hazard and recovery-ratio library (owned by the overlay).
(h) ONE hotkey yield index and choose_hotkey (owned by the overlay).
(i) Event decoder: scalecodec plus per-spec metadata, with V15 runtime-API types for the basket and metagraph calls. Must be verified on Windows.
(j) Shared execution simulator: N+2 fills, limit semantics, failure injection, fee table, impact-persistence options.
(k) Gatekeeper registry and flags.
(l) Flow invariant: dSubnetTAO - injection - chain buys vs dSubnetTaoFlow, checked every block as a health check. SubnetTaoFlow semantics can change in any runtime (open question 14), and four sleeves depend on it.

2. DATA BUDGET (fits the constraints if reads are shared)
Live/paper, one shared head reader:
- per block: 1 universe read, 1 System.Events, 1 get_subnet_to_prune, plus head/finality ≈ 4 RU/block ≈ 29k RU/day;
- plus per-epoch hotkey scans for candidates and daily baskets ≈ 31k RU/day.
That is about 8% of the OnFinality free 400k RU/day, or about 0.35 req/s on a public endpoint. Five independent readers would multiply this, and the backfill shares the same RU budget.
One-off backfill:
- 60-block Era-C snapshots: about 13-25k RU;
- 300-block full dTAO history: about 15-30k RU;
- gate-era per-epoch hotkey panel plus daily key scans: about 11k RU;
- per-block prune replays for 10 prunes: about 1.5k range calls;
- mean-reversion SubnetTaoFlow change-sets: about 0.5-5k calls;
- launch dense windows: about 4k calls.
Total ≈ 60-100k RU, roughly 6-12 h wall-clock at the measured ~3 req/s public rate. Range-call throughput (24.5 s per 100 blocks x 384 keys) is the long pole.
Host constraint: no Docker or WSL, so no own lite or archive node. Exact-event indexing across history is therefore unavailable. Owner, claim and buyer-breadth features must use storage diffs (AlphaV2 positions of known coldkeys) with Taostats as enrichment.

3. HISTORY LIMITS THAT BIND EVERY TEST
- Rank-32 gate regime: about 66 days. Price-EMA regime: about 107 days.
- Valid SubnetTaoFlow from 8,466,531. Basket escrow from 8,765,683. MinerBurned from 8,466,597. SubnetExcessTao from 8,283,784. Exact Balancer math from 8,486,594.
- Spec 475 (2026-10-07) changed emissions and dividends, so all replicas need revalidation before any paper run.
- All five designs draw on the same short sample. Reserve a common untouched forward paper period as the shared holdout, and count total tuned parameters across sleeves (budget about 20) to limit multiple testing.

4. CONFLICTS THE ALLOCATOR MUST RESOLVE
(a) Forced exits. Prune and emission rules differ by sleeve:
- flow: rank_exit 3, rho_exit 1.3, rho_in 2.0;
- momentum: prune_rank_excl 6;
- mean reversion: cushion 0.30/0.15, rank_min 6;
- overlay: K_ENTRY_HARD 5, G_ENTRY 0.5, Tier A/B.
Rule: the overlay is authoritative for forced exits on the whole physical position; sleeves may only be stricter on entries.
(b) Hotkeys. One subnet must use one hotkey: the overlay's choose_hotkey, with take_max set once.
(c) Age and young-subnet policy:
- flow: 45 days since start_call;
- momentum: 30 days since registration, or 90 days / rank 40;
- mean reversion: 90 days;
- Gatekeeper: YOUNG_IMMUNE under 120 days.
Choose one policy table in the allocator.
(d) MinerBurned thresholds vary: 0.2 / 0.5 / 0.3 / 0.35 for entry and 0.60 for exit. Unify them as overlay hard limits plus optional per-sleeve stricter limits.
(e) Emission re-enable: flow may enter after one epoch, mean reversion quarantines for 14 days, and the overlay bans until re-enable + 360 blocks. Sleeve-specific entry rules are acceptable, but the ban semantics must be single-sourced.
(f) Sizing double-counting. Sleeves compute V* from their own alpha_h; the overlay re-haircuts with m_gate, m_trd and m_esc. Pass alpha_h through and apply only pool and exit caps to sleeves that declare their own dilution model.
(g) Cash floors: overlay G_MAX 80%, flow m_mkt, momentum x_max 100%. The overlay's is binding.
(h) Execution contention:
- one in-flight order per netuid and 3 Staking-proxy delegates (nonce lockout after a shield miss);
- a priority queue is needed: Tier A/emission exits > time-critical sleeve entries (mean reversion W_stab, momentum P1) > rebalances;
- the planner needs Rotate (move_stake_limit) and same-subnet MoveStake order types;
- non-urgent orders should follow flow's drain-timing rule;
- virtual netting must also report each sleeve's stand-alone P&L for kill switches.
(i) Determinism. Seed every stochastic piece (overlay MC, bootstraps) from the block hash. Log the features at each decision so paper can be replayed bit-for-bit in backtest.

5. GATING AND SAFETY BOUNDARY
Every design emits Order intents only.
- Enforce by package structure: the strategy, backtest and paper packages must not import bittensor (a CI import check).
- The live adapter is a separate WSL2/Linux process. It is off by default, needs an explicit flag plus config, uses a Staking-proxy delegate, runs under the user's control, and is never driven by this process.
- The designs' pseudocode puts submit_shielded only behind LIVE/LIVE_GATED branches. Those branches should be replaced with a hand-off that writes intents to the adapter's queue.

6. RECOMMENDED BUILD ORDER
1. ChainReader, StateView, store and pool simulator, with replica unit tests against chain at 20 random blocks.
2. Backfill.
3. Risk overlay core (Tier A, backstop, emission-off, caps, modes, planner, execution simulator) plus the Gatekeeper.
4. Flow sleeve: yield and hotkey carry first, then sell load after T3.
5. Momentum MVP behind a flag.
6. Mean-reversion and launch-LCW in shadow/recording mode.
7. Overlay MC, Tier B and allocator refinements after FT1/FT2.
